title: Carpet in Lynnwood Condos: Sound Requirements and HOA Rules
meta: Carpet in Lynnwood condos: what HOA sound rules (IIC ratings, coverage, work hours) really require, which pad passes, and how to get approved. Wills Flooring.
keywords: condo carpet HOA rules, IIC rating carpet condo, condo flooring sound requirements, carpet padding for condos, carpet installation Lynnwood WA

blocks.lead: Most Lynnwood condo HOAs require carpet or an equivalent sound-rated floor over a set share of the unit, set a minimum impact sound rating for the assembly, and ask for written approval before any flooring work starts.
blocks.detail: Carpet over a dense pad is the easiest floor in the building to get approved, because it beats almost any sound rule on its own. The work is reading your CC&Rs, picking a pad the board recognizes, and scheduling around quiet hours. Our labor is published, $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in with a 500 sq ft minimum, which makes the quote you attach to the HOA form easy to read.

blocks.html: Lynnwood has far more condo and townhome units than it did five years ago, and most sit within a few blocks of our showroom on 196th. The buildings around City Center and Alderwood, the older stacked flats off 44th and the new mid-rises by the light rail station share one thing: a neighbor below who can hear your floor. Here is what the rules usually say, what the sound numbers mean, and how to get carpet approved without a letter from the board.

blocks.text: What Lynnwood HOA flooring rules usually say

items.title: A coverage requirement
items.text: Many stacked buildings require a percentage of the unit's floor, or named rooms such as bedrooms and living areas, to stay carpeted or covered with an approved soft surface. Kitchens and baths are normally exempt; some older Lynnwood complexes exempt nothing else.

items.title: A minimum sound rating
items.text: Usually written as an IIC number for the floor assembly, commonly 50 or higher, sometimes with an STC figure for airborne sound. Carpet over pad clears IIC 50 easily, which is why most boards never ask for a test report on carpet.

items.title: An approval process
items.text: Expect an architectural request form, product and pad spec sheets, the installer's license and insurance, sometimes a neighbor sign-off. Approval can take a full meeting cycle, so start weeks ahead.

items.title: Work rules
items.text: Weekday hours, an elevator reservation with pads, a loading zone deposit, and a rule about where the old carpet goes. Ground-floor units and Martha Lake townhomes face fewer of these, since nobody lives below.

blocks.note: IIC measures impact sound such as footsteps; STC measures airborne sound. These are typical lab figures for wood frame, not a promise for your building. Concrete mid-rises start higher.

blocks.text: Which pad passes the board and which one wears out

a.title: Dense rebond or felt, 7/16 in or thinner
items: High density rating is what boards and carpet warranties look for
Firm enough for stairs and traffic lanes inside the unit
Adds a large IIC margin over any hard floor
Spec sheet is easy to attach to the approval form

b.title: Thick, soft, low-density foam
items: Feels plush for a season, then packs down and lets the carpet flex
Voids many carpet manufacturer warranties over a set thickness
Sound gain over a proper dense pad is minor
Some boards reject anything without a published density figure

blocks.html: Condo math is worth doing carefully, because units are small. A City Center two-bedroom with 740 sq ft of bedrooms, hall and living room is 740 × $0.99 = $733 in labor, plus 740 × $0.45 = $333 to pull the old carpet and pad and carry them out. A one-bedroom with 430 sq ft still bills at our 500 sq ft minimum, so that line reads 500 × $0.99 = $495. Carpet and pad are quoted at the estimate, and in a condo the pad is worth paying up for: it is what the board checks and what the neighbor below hears.

items.text: Find the flooring section of your CC&Rs. Note the coverage rule, the IIC or STC minimum, work hours, and whether an architectural request is required.
We measure, look at the subfloor and old pad, bring samples and pull the pad spec sheet that matches your building's number.
Product sheet, pad sheet with density and thickness, our license and insurance, the proposed dates and the priced quote. Some boards also want a floor plan showing the carpeted share.
Once the board signs off, reserve the elevator and loading zone. Our showroom is minutes away, so a narrow window is workable.
Old carpet and pad out, subfloor checked and squeaks screwed down, new pad and carpet in. A two-bedroom unit is one working day inside the HOA's hours.

blocks.text: Mistakes that get a Lynnwood condo owner a violation letter

items: Installing first and asking later. Boards can require removal of an unapproved floor at your expense, and carpet is easy to approve anyway.
Swapping bedroom carpet for hard flooring, then discovering the coverage rule. Carpet in bedrooms and hard surface in the living area is the usual compromise.
Reusing the old pad to save a step. Old pad is compressed, may carry pet odor, and often does not match the spec the board approved.
Ignoring quiet hours. Power stretchers and staple guns are loud. We schedule to the building's window, but the owner has to tell us what it is.
Leaving the old carpet roll in the hallway or by the dumpster. Most Lynnwood complexes fine for that; haul-away is $0.45 per sq ft and includes taking it away the same day.

blocks.title: If you want hard floors instead:
blocks.text: Some Lynnwood boards approve vinyl plank or hardwood in living areas if the underlayment carries a test report meeting the building's IIC minimum. It is a heavier paperwork lift than carpet. See hardwood in condos and vinyl plank in condos before deciding.

items.html: Get the actual rule in writing. Ask the manager for the flooring section, not a summary. The IIC number and coverage share should be in the text.
Ask for the pad's density and thickness on the quote. Those two numbers are what the board checks and what the carpet warranty depends on.
Confirm license and insurance. Nearly every HOA asks. Wills Flooring is licensed and insured and has worked in Lynnwood buildings since 2013.
Measure the elevator and the hallway turns. Carpet arrives in a 12 ft roll, so tight corridors can mean cutting on the loading dock. Fine, if planned.
Pick fiber for the neighbor below too. Denser, lower pile over a dense pad is quieter and wears better than tall plush. Our carpet installation page covers fiber.
Book with the approval cycle in mind. Boards that meet monthly can cost you four weeks. Get the estimate first so the packet is complete on the first try.

faq.q: Can my HOA force me to keep carpet in my Lynnwood condo?
faq.a: Yes, if the recorded CC&Rs include a coverage or sound requirement. Those documents run with the unit and bind every owner. Most boards allow hard floors in living areas over an approved underlayment, but bedrooms above another unit usually have to stay carpeted.

faq.q: What IIC rating does carpet have?
faq.a: Carpet over a dense pad on a wood-frame floor typically tests in the mid 50s to 60s, well above the IIC 50 most Lynnwood buildings require. That margin is why boards rarely ask for a lab report on carpet; the pad spec sheet is usually enough.

faq.q: Do I need HOA approval just to replace carpet with new carpet?
faq.a: Usually yes, at least a notice. Many buildings treat like-for-like carpet as a minor change that gets fast approval, but they still want the installer's insurance, the work dates and confirmation the pad meets spec. Check the rules rather than assuming.

faq.q: Which carpet pad is best for a condo?
faq.a: A dense rebond or felt pad at 7/16 inch or thinner. Density matters more than thickness for both sound and wear. Very thick, soft foam pads feel good briefly, void many carpet warranties and are sometimes rejected by boards because they lack a published density figure.

faq.q: How long does condo carpet installation take?
faq.a: One working day for a typical one or two bedroom Lynnwood unit, tear-out and haul-away included, provided the elevator is reserved and we can work the building's hours. Townhomes with stairs can run into a second morning.

faq.q: Does Wills Flooring handle the HOA paperwork?
faq.a: We supply everything the board asks of the installer: product and pad spec sheets, our license and insurance certificate, and a written quote with published rates and dates. You submit the form, since the HOA relationship is yours, but we make sure the packet is complete first time.
